info.title: Backend API
info.description: FastAPI Backend with Auth, Git & Celery Integration

get.description: Check if auth service is healthy
Get current authenticated user with course information

Get all users with optional filters
- **Requires**: TEACHER or ADMIN role

Search users directly from Keycloak by username, email, or name
- **Requires**: TEACHER or ADMIN role
- Returns users from Keycloak (not local DB)

Response:
- id: Keycloak user ID
- username: Username
- email: Email address
- firstName: First name
- lastName: Last name
- enabled: Account enabled status

Get user by ID
- **Students**: Can only view their own profile
- **Teachers/Admins**: Can view any profile

put.description:
Update a user record.

Profile edits (firstName/lastName/email/username) happen exclusively
in Keycloak; ``UserUpdate`` only carries ``role`` and ``courseId``.
Both are admin-only: ``role`` changes go through
:func:`ensure_change_user_role` (403 with ``{code: "role_required",
required: ["admin"]}``), and ``courseId`` changes require admin too.

get.description:
Get user statistics
- **Owner or Teacher/Admin** can view

Get all courses
- **Students**: Can view all courses
- **Teachers/Admins**: Can view all courses

post.description:
Create a new course
- **Requires**: TEACHER or ADMIN role

A creating teacher is automatically registered as a course-teacher of
the new course via the ``course_teachers`` join table, so the
edit/delete gate passes for them without an extra round trip. Admins
are NOT auto-added (admin rights already cover edit/delete); they can
opt in via ``POST /courses/{id}/teachers/{user_id}``.

get.description:
Get course by ID with all users.

The member list is personal data (e-mail addresses): teachers and
admins may read it, students get 403 (.github#7 F, security review
M-2).

put.description:
Update a course

Only a designated course-teacher of THIS course (row in
``course_teachers``) or an admin may edit; others get 403 with the
structured ``course_edit_forbidden`` payload. 404 takes precedence
over 403 for nonexistent courses.

delete.description:
Delete a course

Only a designated course-teacher of THIS course or an admin may
delete. Members are detached (``users.courseId = NULL``) before the
row goes away — no user account is destroyed; ``course_teachers``
rows cascade away via ON DELETE CASCADE.

get.description:
List the users currently enrolled in ``course_id``.

Teachers and admins only — student rosters are management data.

schema.title: Response List Course Members Courses  Course Id  Users Get

post.description:
Add (or move) a batch of users into ``course_id``.

The frontend's add-modal uses the same Keycloak-backed user search
as the deployment-team picker, so by the time we get here the
user-ids exist in our DB. Returns the post-update member list of
the course so the UI can refresh without a second round trip.

Course-teachers of THIS course and admins only; moving a user out of
another course also needs that right on the other course (.github#7 F,
security review H-1/A-3): nobody pulls someone from a course they do
not manage into their own.

schema.title: Response Add Course Members Courses  Course Id  Users Post

delete.description:
Remove ``user_id`` from ``course_id``.

Returns 404 if the user isn't actually enrolled in this course —
we never silently detach somebody from a different course.
Course-teachers of THIS course and admins only (.github#7 F).

post.description:
Register ``user_id`` as a course-teacher of ``course_id``.

Admin-only. The target user must already exist and have role
``TEACHER`` — adding a student or admin to this table would
contradict the ``is_course_teacher`` gate (which requires
``role == TEACHER``) and create a row that the capability
function silently ignores. We refuse those up-front with a
structured 422.

Idempotent: re-adding an existing pair is a no-op (the composite
primary key catches the duplicate, but we check up-front to keep
the success/no-op path distinct from "user not found").

delete.description:
Revoke ``user_id``'s course-teacher status on ``course_id``.

Admin-only. Returns 404 if the user wasn't a course-teacher of
this course — we never silently delete from a different course.
Note this does NOT remove the user from ``users.courseId``;
course membership and course-teacher status are independent
facets (a teacher can stop teaching a course but stay enrolled
as a regular member, or vice versa).

get.description:
List apps visible to the current user.

Admins see every non-deleted app (full platform view). Everyone else,
including teachers, sees the student-style filter: own apps + public
apps with at least one approved version.

post.description:
Create a new app
- Teachers and admins only (403 ``role_required``, .github#7 F)
- The repository must be public and on an allowed host
  (``APP_GIT_ALLOWED_HOSTS``); 422 otherwise, 403 if it cannot be read
- The stored ``git_link`` is the normalised, credential-free HTTPS URL

get.description:
Get app by ID with available versions.

Soft-deleted apps are still readable here so existing deployments
that still reference them can render their app name, git link,
etc. They just don't show up in the apps list / deploy wizard
(those use the default-filtered ``get_apps``).

The owner and admins see every tag. Everyone else sees the approved
versions whose tag still points to the approved commit; a moved tag
disappears until it is submitted and approved again.

``deploy_version`` is only reported while that version can still be
deployed (its tag exists and points to the approved commit). If the
repository cannot be read, the stored value is reported as it is.

put.description:
Update an app.

``git_link`` is immutable after creation — sending it in the body
returns HTTP 400. Use ``is_private`` to toggle visibility.

Owner OR admin only. An app an admin deactivated (``hidden_by_admin``)
can be made public again only by an admin (403 ``app_hidden_by_admin``
for the owner); an admin doing so lifts the deactivation (.github#7 R).

delete.description:
Soft-delete an app.

Sets ``apps.deleted_at`` instead of removing the row, so any
historical or still-running deployment that points at this app keeps
resolving. The app stops appearing in listings and the deploy wizard;
existing deployments live on until destroyed individually.

Owner OR admin only.

get.description:
Get the variables of an app version from the appstore.yaml in its Git repository

Returns:
- name: Variable name
- type: Variable type (string, number, bool, list, map, etc.)
- description: Variable description
- default: Default value (if any)
- required: Whether variable is required

Reads the commit ``version`` points to now; 404 for an unknown tag,
502 when the repository cannot be read.

schema.title: Response Get App Variables Apps  App Id  Variables Get

get.description:
How ``version`` runs, for the deploy wizard: its scope, egress, access, resources, network.

Same visibility and errors as the variables; 422 (with field paths in
``errors``) for a missing or invalid appstore.yaml.

post.description:
Submit a version tag for admin review, at the commit it points to now.

Owner OR admin only. A REJECTED version, or one whose tag has moved
since its review, can be resubmitted; a PENDING or APPROVED one at the
same commit cannot (409). 422 for a missing or invalid appstore.yaml, 404
for an unknown tag, 502 when the repository cannot be read.

delete.description:
Withdraw a PENDING version submission.

Owner OR admin only. Deletes the approval entry so the version
appears as unsubmitted again.

get.description:
List all version approval entries for an app.

Owner OR admin only.

schema.title: Response List Version Approvals Apps  App Id  Versions Get

get.description: Return all version submissions awaiting admin review, oldest first.

schema.title: Response List Pending Versions Admin Apps Versions Pending Get

post.description:
Approve a submitted version at its submitted commit — makes exactly
that commit deployable by all users (.github#7 G).

- 404: the app or the version submission does not exist.
- 409 ``version_moved``: the tag no longer points to the submitted
  commit; the admin would approve code that was not submitted.
- 409: the version is already approved, or was submitted before
  versions were pinned to commits.
- 422: the submitted commit has no valid appstore.yaml.
- 502: the repository cannot be read; nothing is approved unchecked.
Reject a PENDING version with a mandatory reason.
Revoke a previously APPROVED version with a mandatory reason (sets status to REJECTED).

put.description:
Emergency deactivation: set the app to private so it disappears from
the store immediately. Does not delete the app or its deployments.

Marks it ``hidden_by_admin``: the owner can no longer make it public
again, only an admin can (``PUT /apps/{id}`` with ``is_private: false``,
.github#7 R).

Mark an app as recommended or not. Admin only.

The flag only highlights the app in the catalog; it does not change who
may see or deploy it.

Set the version teachers deploy, or clear it with ``version_tag: null``.

Only a version that is approved for the commit its tag points to now
can be set:

- 404: the app does not exist, or the version has no approval entry.
- 409 ``version_not_approved``: the entry exists but is pending,
  rejected or from before versions were pinned to commits.
- 409 ``version_moved``: the tag points to another commit than the
  approved one; it has to be submitted and reviewed again.
- 502: the repository cannot be read.

The setting is cleared again when the version's approval ends (revoked,
or replaced by a new submission). ``POST /deployments/`` is not bound to
it and still checks the approval of the version it is given.

get.description:
List deployments visible to the caller.

Visibility rules:
  * **Staff** (teachers and admins): deployments they created —
    their own owned set. Cross-user listing is intentional UX: a
    teacher opens an individual deployment via direct link or via
    a student's profile page, not from this index.
  * **Students** (and any non-staff role): deployments they own
    OR are a member of — either via a team mapping or a direct
    ``UserToDeployment`` row.

A ``?scope=course`` branch used to sit here, listing every
deployment whose owner was in a course the caller teaches. It had
no caller in the frontend and no test, it silently ignored
``status_filter``, and its admin arm was a comment block ending in
``pass``. Removed rather than repaired: if the
teacher-inspects-a-student feature comes back it wants its own
endpoint with a working filter and tests, not this.

post.description:
Create a new deployment

Atomicity: a per-user advisory lock serializes concurrent creates of one
user (the workload budget). The deployment row, teams, user mappings,
and the initial PENDING task row are all inserted in a single
transaction, so the user can never end up with a deployment row
that has no matching task. The queue dispatch happens AFTER commit;
if it fails, the task row is flipped to FAILED so the deployment
surfaces an honest error instead of hanging in PENDING forever.

get.description:
Get deployment by ID with full details including:
- User and App relations
- Teams with members
- Latest task status
- Task outputs (the "terraform_outputs" of the result contract)
- Optionally: full logs (use include_logs=true)

delete.description:
Unified delete — destroys the namespace of a pod deployment first.

Restricted to the owner-view (creator, teacher, admin). Members
can read-access the deployment but never tear it down.

get.description:
The workloads of a pod deployment, read live from its namespace.

Owner view (owner, admin); this endpoint is read-only.

post.description: Restart one team's or person's workload (a new pod); its data stays.
Reset one workload: its volume is deleted, it starts from scratch.

Stop an in-flight deployment and clean up everything it created.

Owner-only, same gate as Destroy. Returns ``202 + {task_id,
status: "destroying"}`` so the frontend can stay on the live SSE
view and watch the cleanup run.

Pause a running deployment by scaling its workloads to zero.

Owner-only — same gate as Destroy, because pausing a teammate's
deployment is in practice a denial-of-service against the team.

Returns ``202 + {task_id, status: "pausing"}`` on dispatch. The
frontend reads ``status`` to switch to the live SSE view; the
deployment's effective status is recomputed from the new task
row by ``crud_deployments.get_deployment_status``.
Resume a paused deployment by starting its workloads again.

get.description:
Stream the raw bytes of one wizard-uploaded file back to the owner.

Path components mirror how the upload was indexed:
  * ``var_name`` — the name of the file variable (``type: file`` in appstore.yaml)
  * ``slot_key`` — the inner-map key (``"all"`` for scope=all,
    team name for scope=team, ``Team-User`` composite for scope=user)

Returns 404 if any layer of the lookup misses; the frontend can
therefore probe a slot's existence via this endpoint without
needing a separate metadata response.

Return the calling member's OWN access credentials for a deployment.

The only way to the credentials (no mails, .github#7 I). The full
outputs carry every teammate's credentials and are owner-view only;
a team member — typically a student — gets exactly their own account
entry, matched exactly by ``services.access`` (.github#7 H), plus their
team's VM block. Never a teammate's.

Member-view gate: owner, team member or direct mapping; anyone else
gets 403.

Returns 200 with empty maps when there's no successful deploy yet or
no entry belongs to the caller exactly — the UI renders a "no
credentials yet" state rather than treating it as an error.

Return ONE member's access credentials, e.g. to answer their question.

The only path that hands a member's credentials to somebody else: the
owner view's outputs stay redacted (.github#7 E) and ``my-access``
returns the caller's own entry only. Gated by the operate right
(owner or admin), not the wider owner view, and one member per call:
the credentials leave the server when somebody asks for them, not
with every detail response. Same entry as the member's own
``my-access``, matched exactly by ``services.access`` (.github#7 H).

Never cached and never logged. Empty maps when the user is in none of
the deployment's teams or there is no entry for them.

Live progress + log stream for one deployment as Server-Sent Events.

Streams the events of the deployment's latest task and ends with its
terminal event. Starts with a ``snapshot`` event; for a task that is
already finished (or no task at all) the stream ends right after it.
List all tasks for a deployment the caller has owner-access to.

The teams of ``deployment_id`` the caller may read (all of them with
the owner view, otherwise their own). 403 without access to the

get.description: A team with its members: owner view of the deployment or membership.

get.description:
Aggregate counts for the dashboard KPI strip.

Cheap DB-only aggregates.

Deployments counter MUST mirror the visibility rules of
``GET /deployments`` so the KPI matches what the user actually sees
on the Deployments page:

  * Teacher/Admin: deployments they own.
  * Student:       deployments they own OR are a team member of OR
                   have a direct ``UserToDeployment`` mapping for.

Apps counter MUST mirror the role-branched visibility of
``GET /apps`` (see ``routers/apps.py``):

  * Admin: every non-deleted app — exactly what
    ``crud_apps.get_apps`` returns when called without
    ``user_id``. Admin keeps the plattform-wide view.
  * Teacher/Student: own apps (regardless of ``is_private`` /
    approval state) OR public apps (``is_private = False``)
    with at least one APPROVED version — mirrors
    ``crud_apps.get_visible_apps``. Teacher gets the student-style
    filter.

Soft-deleted rows (``deleted_at IS NOT NULL``) are excluded on both
counters — same as the list endpoints.
Step 1 (GET): the OIDC login initiation from Moodle, parameters in the query string.

post.description:
Step 1 (POST): the same initiation with form-encoded parameters.

Moodle sends this as a POST (observed against a real Moodle 5.x
instance, 2026-09-25) even though the IMS spec allows either GET or
POST for the 3rd-party-initiated login, so both are accepted. Two
routes rather than one for both methods: each gets its own OpenAPI
operation id (one shared id broke the generated frontend types).
Step 3: Moodle POSTs the id_token here after the OIDC dance.

get.description:
Expose this tool's public JWKS.

For the demo the tool does not sign messages back to the platform, so
this returns an empty key set. Replace with actual RSA keys if Assignment
& Grade Services (AGS) or deep linking is needed.

AppRuntimeResponse.title: AppRuntimeResponse
AppRuntimeResponse.description: How one version runs, for the deploy wizard.

AppVariableResponse.title: AppVariableResponse
AppVariableResponse.description:
Shape of one entry in ``GET /apps/{id}/variables``.

Keys match what ``app_spec.spec_variables`` writes to the dict exactly —
the frontend reads ``osType``/``osMode``/``osMulti``/``osScope``/
``varScope``/``fileExtensions`` in camelCase and the rest in
snake/lowercase. Keys are kept verbatim (no auto-aliasing).

CourseMembersUpdate.title: CourseMembersUpdate
CourseMembersUpdate.description:
Body for bulk-adding members to a course.

Course membership lives on ``users.courseId``, so a "member" is a
user-id whose FK is (re-)pointed to this course; an existing
enrollment on another course is overwritten.

DeploymentDetail.title: DeploymentDetail
DeploymentDetail.description: Full deployment details with teams, task info, and outputs

DeploymentFileUpload.title: DeploymentFileUpload
DeploymentFileUpload.description:
Single file uploaded by the teacher in the deploy wizard.

Persisted verbatim into ``userInputVar.terraform`` keyed by the
variable name (and recipient key for team/user scope); the pod
deployer puts it into the workload's files.

``content_b64`` MUST be standard (RFC 4648) base64.

DeploymentOutputs.title: DeploymentOutputs
DeploymentOutputs.description: Outputs of the deploy job - structure depends on app

DeploymentPermissions.title: DeploymentPermissions
DeploymentPermissions.description:
What the caller may do with a deployment, decided by the API.

``owner_view``: tasks, logs, the live stream, infrastructure and the
(redacted) outputs. ``operate``: pause, resume, destroy, redeploy,
cancel and team changes. ``member``: the caller is in one of its teams
and gets their own access through ``my-access``.

DeploymentResourceListResponse.title: DeploymentResourceListResponse
DeploymentResourceListResponse.description:
Wrap the list in an object so we can add cursor/refresh-stamp
metadata later without a breaking API change.

MyAccessResponse.title: MyAccessResponse
MyAccessResponse.description:
A single team member's own access credentials.

Returned by ``GET /deployments/{id}/my-access`` so a member (student)
can see their OWN credentials without the owner-view that gates the
full outputs. Only the caller's own account is ever present.

Both maps use the ``user_accounts`` / ``team_vms`` output shape (one key
each: the member's account and their team's workload)
so the frontend's existing account-matching pipeline consumes this
unchanged. Empty maps mean "no credentials yet" (no successful deploy,
or the app issued no per-user account) — a valid 200, not an error.

PodSetupProgress.title: PodSetupProgress
PodSetupProgress.description: What an app reports about its first-start setup (an ``appstore-progress`` log line).

PodWorkloadSchema.title: PodWorkloadSchema
PodWorkloadSchema.description:
One workload of a pod or kubevirt-vm deployment, read live from the cluster (.github#4).

The name is historic (pods came first); the schema serves both runtimes.

TaskResponse.title: TaskResponse
TaskResponse.description:
A task as the task API shows it to the owner view.

Deliberately without ``tf_state`` and ``outputs`` (.github#7 E): the
state holds every attribute of every resource, generated passwords
included, and the outputs hold every member's credentials. Members get
their own entry through ``my-access``; the owner view's outputs are
redacted (``task_results.redact_sensitive_outputs``).
